samples.summary: `moveTo` now inherits the caret's own stale affinity on paths that hand the current position straight back
samples.evidence: `moveTo(pos)` used to force `'backward'` when no affinity argument was given; it now uses `pos.lineAffinity`. Several callers pass back an object that IS the current `cursor.position`: `Doc.deleteBackward` returns its input `pos` unchanged at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:300 (empty list-item exit), :306 (first block) and :316 (previous block is an HR/page-break), and that value is fed to `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2178; likewise `moveLeft`/`moveRight` return `pos` on clamp (document-level identity return at text-editor.ts:4093/4114/4136/4154) and the selection-collapse branch at text-editor.ts:2963 moves to `normalized.start`/`normalized.end`, endpoints that now carry an endpoint affinity. In each case the caret keeps the reading that was computed for the pre-operation state instead of the deliberate `'backward'` reset the old signature performed. Impact is limited because `resolvePositionPixel` only honours `'forward'` when the offset lands exactly on a wrap boundary, but where it does the caret is drawn one visual line off. No test in the change covers these paths.

samples.summary: Always materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on the caret overrides `buildRects`' deliberate `'forward'` default for a selection START
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261 documents that an endpoint with NO affinity is read from the side the range extends towards — start defaults to `'forward'` precisely so a highlight does not "open on a zero-width sliver of the line above". Selection anchors are routinely taken from the caret (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? this.cursor.position` at text-editor.ts:1794, 2948, 2981, 3000, 3015, 3031), and `Cursor` now stamps `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every position (cursor.ts:26 and moveTo's `?? 'backward'`). So an anchor sitting exactly on a wrap boundary with the caret's backward reading (e.g. End then Shift+Down) now takes the backward branch in `buildRects` instead of the documented forward default, emitting the sliver rect the comment warns about. Visually near-invisible (the rect is zero-width at the line end and the covered region is unchanged), hence nit, but it silently defeats an explicitly-reasoned default.

samples.summary: Peer-label change detection key omits the newly meaningful `lineAffinity`
samples.evidence: `const posKey = `${presence.activeCursorPos.blockId}:${presence.activeCursorPos.offset}`` — now that the peer caret is rendered from `activeCursorPos.lineAffinity` (editor.ts:1588), a peer whose caret visibly jumps between the two visual lines of a wrap boundary keeps the same key, so the name label does not flash for that move. The caret itself still repaints (setPeerCursors runs unconditionally at docs-view.tsx:315), so this is cosmetic only.
